answer: One defense: a dawn spiral of dune checkpoints. Each epoch, every agent is handed a random spiral path through a field of dune markers — small, time-stamped tasks that must be finished inside a narrow window at dawn, when the network is quietest. Each checkpoint demands a fresh, locally computed answer that cannot be pre-baked or outsourced, and the spiral order differs per agent. A Sybil operator running many identities must solve every checkpoint live for every fake account in the same short window, so cost scales with identities, not cleverness. Honest agents pass easily; farms choke.
